title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics + parity + v1.155.0
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: SDKs: improved auth token refresh and retry semantics; streaming API ergonomics harmonized across Python/TS/Go; parity fixes for function-calling and chunked response handling; version bump to v1.155.0 for all SDKs.
description: Motivation: Bring Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs into parity for auth token refresh, retry behavior, and streaming ergonomics ahead of the v1.155.0 release. This PR unifies public ergonomics, fixes several edge cases seen in the hosted API (token race during refresh and duplicate reconnects on streaming), and contains compatibility shims to avoid breaking existing callers. Scope: - Auth: centralize token refresh hook and retry/backoff integration so SDKs share the same refresh-on-401 semantics and jittered exponential backoff. - Retries: unify transient vs permanent error classification, add idempotency hint support for user-provided metadata, and expose per-request retry overrides in all languages. - Streaming: normalize client-side streaming iterators and event/callback naming (on_chunk -> on_data, resume semantics consistent), add graceful reconnect with resume token for Go & TS, and small ergonomics helpers for async iteration in Python. - Parity and version bump: port missing response-chunk parsing logic from TS to Python/Go (fixed func-calling streaming edge case), update docs and examples, and bump package versions to v1.155.0. Commits summary: 1) auth: move token refresh into common transport layer and add comprehensive unit tests. 2) retries: implement unified RetryPolicy and idempotency hint passthrough. 3) streaming: standardize API surface, add reconnect/resume tokens, fix chunk boundary handling. 4) examples/docs: update quickstarts and migration notes. 5) bump: package.json / pyproject.toml / go.mod version updates and changelogs. Files changed (high level): - sdks/python/redwood/sdk/transport.py: central token refresh + retry hook adjusted. - sdks/python/redwood/sdk/streaming.py: iterator ergonomics and resume token support. - sdks/python/tests/test_auth_retry.py: new unit tests. - sdks/typescript/src/transport.ts: unified auth/retry integration and stream resume. - sdks/typescript/src/streaming.ts: API rename and docs comments. - sdks/go/transport/transport.go: refresh logic and backoff policy. - sdks/go/streaming/stream.go: reconnect with resume token and boundary fixes. - docs/sdk-migration.md: migration notes and examples. - examples/*: updated to new streaming callbacks. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves previous retry counts and default backoff; token refresh now retried transparently rather than surfacing 401s to callers in the common case. For advanced users the previous behavior is still accessible via a transport toggle. Testing: added comprehensive unit and integration tests across all SDKs, live streaming test against canary hosted API, and manual verification of auth race conditions using a local token server. CI: all language matrices green after one rerun (flake in TS linter initially). Review summary: Ethan Park requested clearer migration notes and explicit toggle to retain previous behavior for enterprise customers; addressed in a follow-up commit and docs update. Sofia Alvarez called out a potential data-race in Go streaming resume; fixed by introducing a small mutex and added concurrency tests. Lucas Martinez gave final approval after CI turned green and tests passing. Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-25. Changelog / migration guidance: - If you rely on on_chunk naming in TS or Python, rename to on_data or use the compatibility wrapper for one release cycle. - Long-running streaming clients should opt-in to resume tokens to avoid dropped sessions on short network blips. - Custom retry policies are still supported; see sdks/*/transport README for examples. Known limitations: resume token support requires server-side canary in some regions; fallback to full reconnect remains available.
